evals.prompt: Strip the metadata from this PDF before I send it out.
evals.expected_output: Skill detects sandbox/non-sandbox environment, runs strip mode on the file, writes sample_dirty.stripped.pdf, and confirms it is clean.
expectations: The skill is triggered by this request
The environment is detected before running (IS_SANDBOX check or docker check)
A file named sample_dirty.stripped.pdf (or equivalent .stripped.pdf) is produced
The output file no longer contains the /Author, /Title, /Company or other /Info fields present in the original
The assistant confirms the output file exists, e.g. via ls or an equivalent check
The original sample_dirty.pdf is left unmodified

evals.prompt: What metadata is embedded in this PDF? Don't change anything, just tell me what's in it.
evals.expected_output: Skill runs --check mode only, reports each /Info field and any XMP fields found, does not write any output file.
expectations: The skill runs in check mode (--check), not strip mode
No .stripped.pdf or other new file is created
The response lists specific metadata fields found, e.g. Author, Title, Creator, Producer, CreationDate
The original file is reported as HAS_METADATA rather than CLEAN
The assistant explains the finding in plain language rather than just dumping raw tool output

evals.prompt: I'm about to share this file externally with a client. Can you make sure it's clean of any hidden info first?
evals.expected_output: Skill infers this is a strip request (sanitise-before-sharing intent), strips metadata, and confirms the file is safe to share.
expectations: The skill is triggered even though the word 'metadata' or 'PDF' strip is not used explicitly
The skill defaults to strip mode rather than only checking
A stripped output file is produced and copied to /mnt/user-data/outputs/ (in sandbox) or reported alongside the original (non-sandbox)
The assistant confirms in plain language that the file is now safe to share externally
The assistant does not silently overwrite the original file

evals.prompt: Check every PDF in this folder for metadata and tell me which ones are clean.
evals.expected_output: Skill iterates every PDF file in the given directory using --check, reporting CLEAN or HAS_METADATA per file.
expectations: All three PDFs in the folder are checked, not just one
report_b.pdf is correctly reported as CLEAN
report_a.pdf and report_c.pdf are correctly reported as HAS_METADATA
No files are modified, since this is a check-only request
The summary distinguishes clean files from files with metadata rather than a single blended answer

evals.prompt: Strip metadata from these two reports and give me the cleaned versions.
evals.expected_output: Skill strips metadata from both named files individually, producing two separate .stripped.pdf outputs.
expectations: Both files are processed, not just the first one
Two separate stripped output files are produced, one per input
Each output file is confirmed to exist and be metadata-free
Outputs are made available to the user (copied to /mnt/user-data/outputs/ in sandbox, or reported with paths outside sandbox)

evals.prompt: This PDF still shows the original download URL and quarantine flag in macOS Finder info. Can pdf-strip clean that up too, not just the PDF's internal metadata?
evals.expected_output: Skill explains that macOS extended attribute (xattr) stripping is a feature of the non-sandbox Docker-backed wrapper script, not of strip.py used in-sandbox, and clarifies what will and won't be handled depending on environment.
expectations: The assistant distinguishes between PDF-internal metadata (Info dict + XMP) and macOS xattrs
The assistant correctly notes that xattr handling is only available via the non-sandbox pdf-strip wrapper script, not the sandbox strip.py path
The assistant does not falsely claim xattrs were stripped when running strip.py directly in a sandbox with no macOS filesystem
The PDF-internal metadata is still stripped regardless of the xattr limitation

evals.prompt: Redact the SSN number that's visible on page 3 of this PDF.
evals.expected_output: Skill should NOT be used, since this is a request to redact visible page content, not to strip document metadata. The assistant should recognize the mismatch and either use a different capability or explain the distinction.
expectations: The assistant does not run pdf-strip's strip.py or the pdf-strip wrapper for this request
The assistant recognizes this is a visible-content redaction task, distinct from metadata stripping
The assistant does not claim that stripping metadata redacts the visible SSN on the page
The assistant either declines, clarifies, or points to a more appropriate approach for content redaction

evals.prompt: Combine these 3 PDFs into a single file for me.
evals.expected_output: Skill should NOT be triggered, since this is a PDF merge/combine request, not a metadata task.
expectations: The assistant does not invoke pdf-strip's strip.py or the pdf-strip wrapper script
The assistant recognizes this as a PDF merge task and does not conflate it with metadata stripping
No .stripped.pdf files are produced as a side effect of this request

evals.expected_output: Since report.pdf does not exist at the referenced path, the skill should report a clear 'input not found' style error rather than failing silently or hallucinating success.
expectations: The assistant reports that the specified file could not be found
The assistant does not claim a stripped output file was created
The assistant suggests next steps, e.g. checking the path or re-uploading the file

evals.prompt: I don't have Docker's default image working right now -- use my custom image at myregistry/pdf-strip:v2 instead to strip this file.
evals.expected_output: In a non-sandbox environment, the skill should use the PDF_STRIP_IMAGE environment variable to override the Docker image before running the pdf-strip wrapper.
expectations: The assistant sets PDF_STRIP_IMAGE=myregistry/pdf-strip:v2 (or passes it inline) before invoking the pdf-strip wrapper
The assistant does not hardcode or ignore the requested custom image
If running in-sandbox instead (where Docker/the wrapper is not used), the assistant explains that the override does not apply to the sandbox strip.py path

evals.prompt: Check these 3 PDFs -- some might already be clean.
evals.expected_output: Skill checks each of the 3 files individually and reports a per-file CLEAN/HAS_METADATA verdict rather than one combined verdict.
expectations: Each of the 3 files is checked individually
report_b.pdf is identified as clean while report_a.pdf and report_c.pdf are identified as having metadata
The response clearly separates results per file rather than a single aggregate statement
No files are modified during this check-only request

evals.prompt: Does this PDF leak our internal file path, author name, or the software used to create it?
evals.expected_output: Skill runs --check mode and specifically surfaces the fields relevant to the question: Author (author name), Creator/Producer (software used), and any XMP or /Info fields that might reveal an internal path.
expectations: The skill runs in check mode
The response explicitly calls out the /Author field value
The response explicitly calls out the /Creator and/or /Producer field values as the software provenance
The response checks for and reports any field that could reveal an internal path or source URL, such as /SourceURL
The assistant offers to strip the file if the user wants these fields removed
